latest_shares_snapshot.note: Latest quarterly earnings disclosure snapshot. NOT tied to any fiscalYear in 'data' above (those are EDINET annual filings). Reflects post-FYE corporate actions (stock splits, buybacks, cancellations, new issuances) up to the disclosure_date. Two market-cap formulas: (1) Industry-standard cap (Yahoo!Finance, Bloomberg style) = shares_outstanding × current price. (2) Treasury-excluded cap = shares_outstanding_excluding_treasury × current price; this field is server-side COALESCE'd (treasury_shares=null treated as zero) so no client-side null fallback is required. Note: this is treasury-excluded only, NOT free float in the strict sense (which also excludes cross-shareholdings, parent-company holdings, and insider holdings). For point-in-time fiscal-year analysis, keep using sharesIssued in each annual row. IMPORTANT — splitAdjustmentFactor lag: this snapshot reflects post-FYE stock splits immediately (next-day after quarterly disclosure), but the per-row split_adjustment_factor in 'data' above is sourced from split_events (5-layer detection: yuho text-block regex, sharesIssued YoY inference, decision-disclosure capture, prior_inferred from XBRL Current/Prior ratio, and manual override). For post-FYE splits, split_adjustment_factor typically updates within 1–2 business days of the decision-disclosure capture, or upon next annual filing — until then the latest annual row may show split_adjustment_factor = 1.0 while the snapshot already reflects the post-split share count. To detect this transient state client-side, compare snapshot.shares_outstanding / data[-1].sharesIssued: if the ratio is an integer near 2/3/4/5/10 (±2%) and data[-1].split_adjustment_factor = 1.0, treat the row as in-flight and rely on snapshot.shares_outstanding for market-cap. We monitor this invariant daily with an internal alert. Please report any persistent mismatch (>5 business days) to edinetdb@cabocia.jp. See docs/field-notes/latest_shares_snapshot.md.
